limitations: The single-context probe measured exp case 8 only; it has no case 1, other-case, other-operator, or long-run qualification.
No method study measures an optimized candidate against baseline; A/A role ratios are measurement diagnostics, not optimization speedups.
Study order was sequential rather than randomized across repeated independent runs; process lifetime, runtime initialization, warmup repetition and temporal state changed together.

No subphase timestamps separate aclInit, context allocation, input preparation, host startup, warmup or cleanup; neither lifecycle residual nor log mtime identifies a unique hardware/runtime root cause.
Graph replay changes event scope and measurement binary/harness. Absolute times across methods cannot be pooled or interpreted as candidate benefit.
Advisory locks and recorded CPU affinity control cooperating collection jobs; this analysis has no full-system scheduler/clock/power trace proving absence of all external interference.
Single-context fixed output paths retain and verify only the last process output per role, not every overwritten intermediate process output.
